one_line: Chief minister and organiser of the paik system under Ahom king Pratap Singha in early 17th‑century Assam.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, lean but sturdy build, the wiry presence of a seasoned administrator used to field inspections and court debates.
appearance.face: Oval face with a slightly sharp jaw, medium-brown Assamese complexion, high cheekbones, straight nose, faint crow’s feet at the eyes, trimmed moustache with a short downward turn, calm default expression with focused, measuring eyes that hint at strict discipline.
appearance.hair: Straight black hair with a few grey strands, pulled back into a small low knot at the back of the head; front hair combed neatly with no fringe; wears a simple pale-cream cloth turban wrapped close to the skull with a narrow red border at the edge, knotted at the back so it sits low and practical rather than tall or ornate.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate early 17th‑century upper-Assam official attire: a long-sleeved knee-length cotton tunic (like a kurta) in muted off-white with a slightly high round collar and side slits, over a wrapped lower garment (dhoti-style) in deep indigo blue tied firmly at the waist and falling to the ankles; over the tunic he wears a sleeveless waistcoat-like jacket in dull maroon handloom fabric with subtle vertical weave texture, cut straight and close to the body; a narrow woven sash in mustard yellow is tied diagonally from left shoulder to right hip, hinting at office; simple dark-brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery—only a small pair of plain gold ear-rings close to the lobes and a single copper bangle on the right wrist—keeping him practical and unostentatious yet recognisably high-ranking.
appearance.signature: A rolled bundle of palm-leaf or paper manuscripts bound with a red cord held in his left hand, with the top leaf partly unfurled showing faint script lines, and a slender bamboo staff in his right hand used as both walking stick and symbol of authority.

ref_desc: Momai Tamuli Borbarua is a lean, middle-aged Assamese man with an oval medium-brown face, neat black hair in a low knot under a pale-cream turban, wearing an off-white tunic, deep indigo dhoti, maroon sleeveless jacket, mustard sash, dark-brown sandals, small gold earrings, and carrying a rolled manuscript bundle and bamboo staff in a muted off-white, indigo, maroon, mustard and dark-brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model of Momai Tamuli Borbarua, an early 17th-century Assamese chief minister: a lean, middle-aged man with an oval medium-brown face, high cheekbones, trimmed moustache and calm, assessing eyes; his straight black hair, lightly streaked with grey, is pulled into a small low knot and wrapped with a simple pale-cream cloth turban with a narrow red edge, fitting close to the head. Dress him in a modest, long-sleeved knee-length off-white cotton tunic with a slightly high round collar and side slits, over a wrapped deep indigo blue dhoti that falls to his ankles, and add a straight, close-fitting sleeveless maroon handloom waistcoat over the tunic. A narrow mustard-yellow woven sash runs diagonally from his left shoulder to his right hip, hinting at his administrative office, and he wears dark-brown leather sandals. Keep jewellery minimal: only small plain gold earrings and a single copper bangle on his right wrist. Place a rolled bundle of palm-leaf or paper manuscripts bound with a red cord in his left hand and a slender bamboo staff in his right, posing him upright as if inspecting paiks and roads, with an expression of disciplined authority. Use a restrained palette of off-white, deep indigo blue, maroon, mustard yellow and dark brown, with clean anime linework and clear views of face, hair, costume and accessories for consistent redrawing from multiple angles.
